title: Real-time Media Communication (RTC) Architecture
method: code read against every statement of the specifications on the project page; statements a component cannot meet by construction marked absent by group

reasons: a specification or code outside the audit that could not be read

swapserver.name: SWAP server (WebRTC Signalling Function of the RTC AS, RTC-4s)

swapclient.name: SWAP client library (signalling side of an RTC endpoint, RTC-4s)

af.name: RTC AF (Provisioning, Configuration and Network Support Functions; none exists)

ice.name: ICE Function, STUN and TURN (none exists)

rtcas.name: Other RTC AS functions: Media, Application-supporting Web, Transport Gateway, Interworking (none exists)

cases.what: The server accepts WebSocket upgrades only on the path /3gpp-swap/v1 (default; configurable).
The server runs SWAP messages over a WebSocket server attached to an HTTP or HTTPS server and relays between endpoints.
The server relays connect messages using the registered matching criteria and other messages using the target identifier, and keeps the source-to-connection mapping.
Messages the server originates carry a source identifier (its own UUID), and incoming messages without a source identifier are rejected as malformed.
The server generates its own source identifier as a random UUID v4; it does not check that incoming identifiers are random.
The server uses one source identifier, generated at construction, for all messages it originates for its lifetime.
A message whose source identifier differs from the one first seen on that WebSocket connection is dropped without a response.
Incoming messages with a source identifier shorter than 10 characters are rejected as malformed, and the server's own identifier is a 36-character UUID.

requirements.name: Common message fields / Message Identifier (messge_id)

cases.case: Message identifier is a sequence number
cases.what: Messages the server originates take their message identifier from a per-source counter starting at 1.
The message identifier counter is kept per source identifier, and the server assigns identifiers only for messages it originates; relayed messages keep the sender's identifier.
Server-originated messages use a counter that starts at 1 and only increases; incoming identifiers are required to be integers of at least 1 but monotonic growth is not checked.

noted: Incoming monotonic increase is not verified by the server.

cases.what: The server lower-cases the message type before validation and dispatch, so any letter case is accepted.

requirements.name: Register message / Parameters

cases.what: The server accepts a criterion of type qos at registration and in connect and matches it by exact equality of type and value; it does not interpret the QoS description.
A connect with several criteria selects only endpoints that registered all of them.
Among matching endpoints the server first keeps those with the most registered criteria and only then picks one at random, so selection is not random over all matches.

noted: Spec also says an endpoint registered without a requested criterion is deprioritized; the code excludes such endpoints instead (findMatches requires all criteria).

requirements.name: Response message / Description

cases.what: Every register, connect, accept, reject, update, close and application message gets an ack or error response, except a changed-source message, which the specification says to ignore.
Responses carry type 'ack' or 'error'.
After forwarding connect, accept, reject, update or application to the target, the server sends an ack to the source.

cases.case: Error when error or target unknown
cases.what: Invalid JSON, schema failures, no match and an unknown target on connect, accept, reject, update and application get an error response, but close to an unknown target is only skipped and acked, and for a connected-but-unregistered target the forwarding step returns silently and an ack follows (accept, reject, update, close, application).
The request field of ack and error responses is the message identifier of the received message.
Every error response carries a description made of the error title and detail.

noted: Messages of type response are silently dropped (line 183). An error for unparseable JSON uses placeholder -1 values for target and request.
Forwarding silently does nothing when the target has not registered (line 270), yet the ack is still sent.
For unparseable JSON no identifier exists and -1 is used.

cases.what: The server sends only 'ack' and 'error' as response type.
The server relays an update message from any endpoint to its target and acks it.
The server requires target and sdp in an update and relays the SDP unchanged, without interpreting media changes.
An update is relayed like any other and leaves the server-side session active.
A close message is relayed to the target, removes the session from the server's active sessions and is acked.
The server accepts a close message from either side of a session, and also sends a close to the peer when a connection drops.
The server relays update messages for partial teardown and keeps the session.
The server relays application messages between endpoints and acks them.

requirements.name: SWAP / Protocol operation

cases.what: Each request the server receives is acked after it has been processed and forwarded.
The server answers with an error response when a message cannot be processed or forwarded.
The error response is an ordinary SWAP response whose description text combines the Problem Details title and detail; no Problem Details object with type, title and status is sent.
The server identifies itself with a UUID and refuses a second open connection that claims a source identifier already in use.
The server's own source identifier is a UUID v4.

Every server-originated message is a SwapMessage with version, source_id, message_id and message_type set in the constructor, and incoming messages without them fail the schema and get an error; the field is named source_id (as in the annex JSON schema), the prose says 'source'.
cases.conflict: Clause 13.2.4.7: 'Every message shall contain the common message fields: source, message_id, and message_type.' versus the JSON schema TS26113_SWAPMessage.json, which names the property source_id and requires version, source_id and message_id.

cases.what: Messages the server originates carry its own identifier, and relayed messages are forwarded unchanged so the sender's identifier stays.
The server generates a UUID v4 at construction and uses it as the source of every message it originates.

noted: Messages of type response are dropped without an ack (line 183).
Problem Details objects with the Table 13.2.4.6-1 type URIs are built but only the title is used, in the description string.
The field is named source_id in the code and the JSON schema; the clause text calls it source.

requirements.name: Procedures for media content and signalling transport / Signalling (RTC-4s) procedures

cases.what: The client library takes the server host, port and prefix from its constructor options; it does not read a Service Access Information message or any swapEndpoints list.

requirements.name: SWAP / Protocol and version identification

cases.what: The client builds the WebSocket URI path ending in /3gpp-swap/v1, without a trailing slash.
The client opens the WebSocket with the subprotocol 3gpp.SWAP.v1, so the header is sent in the upgrade request.

noted: The statement text shows a trailing slash; clause 13.2.3 says a URI should not contain one, and the client follows 13.2.3.

requirements.name: SWAP / Transport

cases.what: The client carries SWAP messages over a WebSocket connection to a SWAP server.
The client only opens outgoing WebSocket connections and cannot listen for an incoming connection request.
Connect messages carry the matching criteria and other messages carry the target identifier, which the server uses to relay.

noted: Only the endpoint-to-server form is used; the client always initiates the WebSocket connection.
The library's SwapServer class could be run inside an endpoint, but SwapClient does not use it.

requirements.name: SWAP / State machine

cases.case: Wait for ICE gathering before offer
cases.what: The helper that creates the offer waits for ICE gathering to complete before returning the SDP; connectOffer itself sends the offer it is given without checking.

noted: The helper is not wired into SwapClient; an application that calls connectOffer directly must wait itself (the demo page does).

requirements.name: Common message fields / Source (source)

cases.what: Every message the client builds carries the client's source identifier.
The client generates a random UUID v4 as its source identifier unless the application supplies one.
The client fixes its source identifier at construction and uses it for every message.
A generated identifier is 36 characters, and messages with a source identifier shorter than 10 characters fail validation when serialised.

noted: An application-supplied identifier is used as given.

cases.case: Message id is a sequence number
cases.what: Each message gets the next integer from a counter.
The counter is kept per source identifier and assigned by the sending client.
Message ids start at 1 and increase by one for each message; validation requires an integer of at least 1.
Incoming and validated message types are lower-cased before use, so any letter case is accepted.
The client can send a register message with a list of matching criteria.
The client can send a criterion of type qos with any value.
The client sends several criteria together in one register or connect message.
The client passes criteria values through unchecked and builds no processing criterion.
The connect message carries the offer SDP supplied by the application.
The connect message always carries a matching_criteria array, empty if the application gives none.
Each criterion must be an object with a type and a value, checked when the message is serialised.

requirements.name: Accept message / Description

cases.what: The client emits connect and update events, and the application accepts by calling accept, which sends an accept message.
accept puts the answer SDP supplied by the application in the accept message.
On a received close the client updates its state, removes the session and emits a close event, but does not send an accept message itself.

cases.case: No SDP in accept to close
cases.what: accept(target) without an answer sends an accept message with no SDP.

noted: The application decides to accept; the library does not reply by itself.
The application can call accept(target) afterwards.

cases.what: The accept message carries the answer SDP in the answer field.

requirements.name: Update message / Description

cases.what: The client can send an update message to its peer.
The update message carries the SDP given by the application, which may describe added, changed or removed streams.
The client emits an update event, and the application accepts by calling accept.
update sends any SDP, so it can carry a half-close; the library has no dedicated half-close function.
close(target) sends a close message to end the session.

noted: The application decides to accept; the library does not reply by itself.

cases.what: The application can reject by calling reject, which sends a reject message.

A reject always carries a description (schema requires target and description), but the reference to the offer or update is optional: SwapClient.reject sets request only if the application passes it and never takes it from the received message.
The reference to the rejected message is included only when the application passes it; it is optional in the client and in message validation.

requirements.name: Close message / Description

cases.what: The client can send a close message to its peer.
On a received close the client removes the session and emits close, and sends no accept message itself.
update sends any SDP, so it can carry a partial teardown; the library has no dedicated function.

noted: The application can call accept(target) afterwards.

requirements.name: Application message / Description

cases.what: sendApp sends application messages with a type and a value, and received ones are emitted as application events.
The application message carries a type, and validation requires it.
The client has no list of supported application types and emits every received application message to the application, without rejecting any.

noted: The application can call reject itself.

cases.what: The type is passed through unchecked; any non-empty string is accepted.

requirements.name: SWAP / Protocol operation

cases.case: Source identifier is a unique string
cases.what: The client's source identifier is a UUID string, unique to the client.
The client generates its source identifier as a random UUID v4.

SwapMessage sets version, source_id, message_id and message_type on every client message, serialize validates them, the schema requires them for all types, and they stay in the clear when the payload is encrypted; the field is named source_id (schema) where the prose says 'source'.
cases.conflict: Clause 13.2.4.7: "Every message shall contain the common message fields: source, message_id, and message_type." Annex schema TS26113_SWAPMessage.json: required ["version", "source_id", "message_id"].

cases.what: Every message the client sends carries the client's own source identifier.

noted: The field is named source_id in the code and the annex schema; the clause text calls it source.

requirements.name: WebRTC signalling protocol / WebSocket URI structure

cases.case: Host is a service provider FQDN
cases.what: The client takes the host from its options and uses it unchecked; it does not build or check an FQDN.

noted: The URI always includes the port.

requirements.name: WebRTC signalling protocol / Protocol and version identification

cases.what: The protocol and version are fixed by the request path of each WebSocket upgrade, and only the v1 path is served.
Upgrade requests are accepted or refused according to the request path.
The served path /3gpp-swap/v1 follows the pattern protocol name then version, and a deployment may set another path through the path option.

requirements.name: WebRTC signalling protocol / WebSocket URI structure

cases.what: The server serves the path /3gpp-swap/v1, that is protocolName 3gpp-swap and protocolVersion v1.
When the server is configured for TLS it is created as an HTTPS server and is announced as a wss URL.

The server takes a path option (default /3gpp-swap/v1) and hands it to the WebSocket server, so a deployment can serve under a prefix by giving /prefix/3gpp-swap/v1; there is no separate prefix option and no check that it starts with '/'; the reference server application does not expose it.
The protocol name in the path is the string 3gpp-swap.
The version segment in the path is v1.
The version segment is the letter v followed by the number 1.
The path the server serves and announces has only the name and version segments after the root.
The path the server serves and announces has no trailing slash.

cases.case: "protocolRoot" shall be a concatenation of the following parts:
cases.what: The server binds the WebSocket upgrade to the path /3gpp-swap/v1 (the path option can carry a prefix, but the reference server application never passes one); the wss scheme depends on a configuration option, and the server announces its URI without any deployment prefix; the protocolRoot composition itself is a URI the client builds, so the server only partly meets the wss and optional-prefix parts.

noted: Path option at is used as given.
A query string on the upgrade request is ignored when the path is matched.

requirements.name: WebRTC signalling protocol / Protocol and version identification

cases.what: Each WebSocket connection uses a URI built with the version v1, so the version is set per connection.
The client identifies protocol and version in the WebSocket URI path of the upgrade request.
The URI is scheme, authority, optional prefix, /3gpp-swap/v1, as in clause 13.2.3.
The scheme is wss unless the application sets secure to false, which gives ws.

requirements.name: WebRTC signalling protocol / WebSocket URI structure

cases.what: The URI is root, then protocol name, then version.
The scheme is wss by default.
When the application sets secure to false the scheme is ws.
The URI has :// between scheme and authority.
An optional prefix is added with one leading slash and its end slashes removed.
The protocol name is 3gpp-swap.
The URI carries the version v1.
The version is written as v1, the letter v and the number 1.
The URI has no other parts than root, name and version (no query or fragment).
The URI the client builds has no trailing slash; trailing slashes of the prefix are removed.

cases.case: "protocolRoot" shall be a concatenation of the following parts:
cases.what: The client builds protocolRoot as scheme (wss by default, ws when the secure option is switched off), "://", host and port, and an optional prefix normalised to start with a single "/", followed by /3gpp-swap/v1; the constructor of WebSocketTransport calls it and the result is used to open the connection.

requirements.name: Media-centric transport interface (RTC-4, RTC-12) / Signalling exchange (RTC-4s)

cases.case: This signalling information shall be exchanged over a full-duplex reliable WebSocket ...
cases.what: WebSocketTransport opens the connection with the platform WebSocket or the ws library, subprotocol 3gpp.SWAP.v1, and sends and receives all SWAP messages over it, queuing while not open and reconnecting on close.

requirements.name: Media-centric transport interface (RTC-4, RTC-12) / Signalling exchange (RTC-4s)

cases.case: This signalling information shall be exchanged over a full-duplex reliable WebSocket ...
cases.what: SwapServer creates a ws WebSocketServer on its HTTP(S) server and exchanges all SWAP JSON messages over the accepted full-duplex WebSocket connections (receive on message, send with ws.send), with ping/pong liveness.
